scenes.dialogue: You walk into a police station on your own at eleven in the morning, but the police record your arrest only at night. When does the twenty four hour clock start?
scenes.shown: You walk into a police station on your own at eleven in the morning, but the police record your arrest only at night. When does the 24-hour clock start?

scenes.dialogue: The Constitution says an arrested person must reach a Magistrate within twenty four hours. This man reached one only the next evening. So was he late or not?
scenes.shown: The Constitution says an arrested person must reach a Magistrate within 24 hours. This man reached one only the next evening. So was he late or not?

scenes.dialogue: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On second November, twenty twenty six, Honourable Justice S Vishwajith Shetty of the Karnataka High Court ruled.
scenes.shown: Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On 2 November 2026, Honourable Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty of the Karnataka High Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: After his wife's death, police registered a case against a man and his parents. Two days later, he surrendered to the police at eleven in the morning.
The police showed his arrest only at nine forty five that night. He was produced before the Magistrate the next day, at five forty five in the evening.
scenes.shown: The police showed his arrest only at 9:45 that night. He was produced before the Magistrate the next day, at 5:45 in the evening.

scenes.dialogue: His counsel argued he was in police custody from eleven in the morning, so the twenty four hours had run out, breaching Articles Twenty One and Twenty Two.
scenes.shown: His counsel argued he was in police custody from 11 in the morning, so the 24 hours had run out, breaching Articles 21 and 22.

scenes.dialogue: The State said he came on his own but did not cooperate, so he was not arrested at once. Merely sitting in a police station, it argued, is not an arrest.
Before I tell you what the High Court decided, a quick request: follow LawWorld, and try India's all in one A I platform for advocates at lawworld dot A I.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? The twenty four hours run from the moment liberty is actually curtailed, not from the arrest time the police write down.
scenes.shown: Finally, what did the High Court decide? The 24 hours run from the moment liberty is actually curtailed, not from the arrest time the police write down.

scenes.dialogue: Detention for questioning is unknown to law. He was held from eleven in the morning, so the arrest was vitiated, and he was granted bail with conditions.
